title: CSS Quiz
description: Fourteen questions covering the whole CSS tutorial: syntax and linking, selectors, colours and units, the box model, typography, display, positioning, flexbox, grid, responsive design and the cascade.

questions.question: What is the main job of CSS in a web page?
questions.explanation: CSS controls presentation: colours, fonts, spacing, layout and motion. Structure is HTML's job and behaviour is JavaScript's.
options: Describing the structure and meaning of the content
Describing how the content looks and is laid out
Reacting to user actions such as clicks

questions.question: A property and its value together, such as `color: red;`, form a ___.
questions.explanation: A declaration is one property-value pair. Several declarations between curly braces form a declaration block, and a selector plus a block form a rule.

questions.question: Which method lets many pages share a single CSS file that the browser downloads once and caches?
questions.explanation: An external stylesheet referenced with `<link rel="stylesheet" href="…">` is fetched once and reused by every page that links to it. Inline styles and style elements are part of each page.
options: The style attribute on each element
A style element in each page
A link element pointing to an external stylesheet

questions.question: What colours are the Home and Docs links?
questions.explanation: Home matches both rules; they have the same specificity (0-1-1), so the later one, green, wins. Docs sits inside a div, so only the descendant rule `.menu a` matches it: blue.
questions.code:
Home
Docs

questions.question: `#ff0000`, `rgb(255 0 0)` and `hsl(0 100% 50%)` all describe the same pure red.
questions.explanation: They are three notations for one colour: full red with no green or blue, which in HSL is hue 0 at full saturation and medium lightness.

questions.question: Which unit is always relative to the root element's font size?
questions.explanation: `rem` stands for root em. `em` is relative to the current (or parent) font size, `%` to the containing block and `vw` to the viewport width.

questions.question: How wide is the visible box, from the outer edge of its left border to the outer edge of its right border?
questions.explanation: Under `content-box` the width covers the content only: 200 + 20 + 20 (padding) + 5 + 5 (border) = 250px. The margin is outside the border and does not count.

questions.question: The `line-___` property sets the vertical distance between lines of text and is best written as a unitless number such as 1.5.
questions.explanation: `line-height: 1.5` means one and a half times the element's own font size, and because the factor is inherited, headings and paragraphs each get a proportional value.

questions.question: What is the difference between `display: none` and `visibility: hidden`?
questions.explanation: `display: none` removes the box from the layout entirely, so nothing is reserved for it. `visibility: hidden` keeps the box's space but does not paint it. Both hide the element from screen readers.
options: display: none removes the element from the layout; visibility: hidden keeps its space
visibility: hidden removes the element from the layout; display: none keeps its space
display: none only works on block elements

questions.question: The badge should sit in the top-right corner of its card, but it does not move at all. What is wrong?
questions.explanation: Offsets such as `top` and `right` only apply to positioned elements. The badge still has the default `position: static`, so they are ignored. Add `position: absolute;` to the badge and `position: relative;` to the card.
options: top and right need percentage units
The badge is still position: static, so the offsets are ignored
The colour must be declared before the offsets

questions.question: In a flex container with `flex-direction: row`, which property aligns the items along the vertical (cross) axis?
questions.explanation: `align-items` controls the cross axis; in a row container that is the vertical direction. `justify-content` distributes items along the main axis.

questions.question: `grid-template-columns: ___(3, 1fr);` creates three equal-width columns.
questions.explanation: `repeat(count, tracks)` repeats a track definition; `repeat(3, 1fr)` is the same as `1fr 1fr 1fr`.

questions.question: Without the viewport meta tag, mobile browsers lay the page out at a desktop-like width and zoom out, so width-based media queries do not behave as expected.
questions.explanation: That is why `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` belongs in the head of every page: it makes the CSS viewport match the device's real width.

questions.question: All four selectors match the same element and set the same property. Which one wins?
questions.explanation: Specificity compares ids first. `#main` scores 1-0-0, and a single id beats any number of classes (`.a.b.c` is 0-3-0, `div.a.b.c` is 0-3-1) and any number of type selectors (`div p a span` is 0-0-4).
